壌.meaning: A launderette runs out of room, so the owner buys the empty patch of <part>soil</part> next door and dumps the overflow <part>laundry pile</part> on it. Socks sprout like weeds and shirts lie in rows. The neighbours call it the sock farm, but on the deeds it's just a <kanji>lot</kanji>.
壌.on: A <sound>jo</sound>ey peeks out of a stretched sweater in the pile and gives a long, slow yawn.
壌.kun: The dust makes it sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and it drops its <sound>chee</sound>se in the dirt.

腎.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, a <part>servant</part> stands at the castle's back gate and strains every barrel of wine from the cellar through a <part>pretzel</part> held up like a sieve. Clean wine goes back in, the dregs go down the drain. The castle doctor says he works just like a <kanji>kidney</kanji>.
腎.on: On his tea break he chews a knobbly root of <sound>gin</sound>ger to stay awake.

詮.meaning: A <part>speech</part> bubble floats over a family dinner, and the <part>whole</part> table keeps stuffing words into it: Gran's point, Dad's reply, the dog's bark. By dessert it's so full it pops all over the pudding. That was one long <kanji>discussion</kanji>.
詮.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try stands by the door with a stopwatch and rings a bell when anyone talks too long.
詮.kun: Gran points at the soggy pudding: '<sound>Sen</sound>d it back, then we'll talk.'

雌.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> moves into a café's <part>spoon rack</part> and lays three eggs in the soup spoons. The cook tiptoes round her all week and hangs a sign on the rack: 'Mother at work.' Hens, queens and this little bird have one thing in common: all <kanji>feminine</kanji>.
雌.on: The cook props a toy <sound>shi</sound>eld in front of the rack to keep off the soup splashes.
雌.kun: When the chicks hatch, he leaves the mother a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon and a roll of <sound>su</sound>shi.

抄.meaning: A diver drops an <part>anchor</part> into a sunken library and hauls it back up with a <part>few</part> soggy pages stuck to its hook, just the best bits of the best books. She dries them on deck and binds them into a thin booklet: an <kanji>extract</kanji>.
抄.on: That night she reads them aloud to the crew in a one-woman <sound>show</sound> that goes on and on.

艶.meaning: A <part>hermit crab</part> finds a <part>bountiful</part> heap of nail polish bottles washed up on the beach. It paints its shell coat after coat until it shines like a wet cherry, and every gull flies down to check its own reflection. Very <kanji>glossy</kanji>.
艶.on: A boat <sound>en</sound>gine roars past, and the crab admires itself in the rainbow of the oily wake.
艶.kun: The fumes make it sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', so it buffs the shell with a scrap of <sound>ya</sound>rn instead.

惧.meaning: A handyman hears a creak in the attic at midnight. His <part>heartbeat</part> thumps so hard that the <part>tool</part> belt round his waist rattles: hammers, pliers, the lot. He climbs one step at a time, sweating with <kanji>dread</kanji>. It's a squirrel.
惧.on: The squirrel is sitting on a stolen <sound>goo</sound>die bag, guarding it with both paws.
惧.kun: He backs into a toy <sound>o</sound>ctopus, shrieks, and lands on the old <sound>so</sound>fa.

賂.meaning: A gull judges the sandcastle contest. <part>Each</part> sand sculptor slips her a juicy <part>shellfish</part> under the table, and somehow every single castle wins first prize. The whole beach runs on the <kanji>bribe</kanji>.
賂.on: A <sound>ro</sound>dent under the table eats half of them before she notices.
賂.kun: She eyes the last shellfish and shrugs: '<sound>My</sound>, <sound>nah</sound>... oh, go on then.'

駒.meaning: A <part>horse</part> at the county fair learns one <part>phrase</part>, 'Carrot, please!', and says it to everyone it meets. It only comes up to their knees, so people laugh and hand over carrots all day. Not a big horse: a <kanji>pony</kanji>.
駒.on: At noon a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo pops out of the fair clock and tries to steal one of its carrots.
駒.kun: Its rider, a <sound>ko</sound>ala in a straw hat, shares the carrots with its <sound>ma</sound>ma.

唾.meaning: A sleepy trumpet player nods off in the middle of a concert, <part>mouth</part> open, lower lip starting to <part>droop</part>. A long silver thread slides down the horn and onto the conductor's shoe. That isn't music: it's <kanji>saliva</kanji>.
唾.on: A <sound>du</sound>ck in the front row quacks, deeply offended.
唾.kun: He wakes with a sneeze, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and wipes his horn on a <sound>ba</sound>r towel.

殉.meaning: A sand knight guards a castle on the beach all <part>season</part>, never stepping back from the tide. When the last big wave comes, he melts where he stands, leaving only his driftwood <part>bones</part> on the spot. The crabs line up to salute his <kanji>martyrdom</kanji>.
殉.on: They plant a little <sound>jun</sound>iper bush where he fell.

旬.meaning: A greengrocer tries to <part>wrap</part> the <part>sun</part> in brown paper so he can keep it in the shop and ripen strawberries all year. By Friday it has burned through the paper and floated home. Fruit only comes in its <kanji>season</kanji>.
旬.on: For winter he settles for <sound>jun</sound>iper berries, which keep for months.

踪.meaning: A monk vanishes from the mountain temple of his <part>religion</part> overnight. All the others find is the print of one bare <part>foot</part> in the snow, pointing towards the bakery. That one print is all that <kanji>remains</kanji> of him: their only clue.
踪.on: The print smells of <sound>so</sound>ap: he left fresh from a long bath.
踪.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' says the abbot, spotting a <sound>to</sound>ffee wrapper beside it.

虜.meaning: A <part>male</part> fiddler busks in the square, and a <part>tiger</part> sits down in front of him, purring. Whenever the music stops, the tiger growls. Sixteen hours later the fiddler is still playing. He is the tiger's <kanji>captive</kanji>.
虜.on: Between tunes the tiger lets him sip one tiny glass of <sound>Rio</sound>ja.
虜.kun: He tries to sneak off by tossing a <sound>to</sound>ffee as a decoy, but the tiger <sound>ree</sound>ls him back and hugs him like a <sound>ko</sound>ala.

蜜.meaning: Every summer something golden drips from the ceiling onto the breakfast table. Up in the <part>attic</part>, one busy <part>insect</part> has built a wall of wax rooms from beam to beam. Dad fits a little tap to the beam, and now they pour <kanji>honey</kanji> straight onto their toast.
蜜.on: Next morning the insect <sound>meets</sound> Dad on the stairs and hands him a bill.

暫.meaning: A gardener gives a tall sunflower a <part>beheading</part> with her shears so it won't block the <part>sun</part> from her tomatoes. A week later the stalk has grown a new head, just as big. Her fix only worked <kanji>temporarily</kanji>.
暫.on: The sunflower stands taller than ever, nodding like a proud <sound>czar</sound> <sound>n</sound>ow.
暫.kun: '<sound>She</sound>'ll be back,' sighs the gardener, hanging up the shears. '<sound>Bah</sound>!'

詔.meaning: The emperor has lost his voice, so he teaches his <part>speech</part> to a parrot. It flies over the land with a <part>call</part> so loud the rice bends: 'Everyone must nap after lunch!' Nobody argues with an <kanji>imperial edict</kanji>.
詔.on: The parrot turns it into a little <sound>show</sound>, dancing on every rooftop as it squawks.
詔.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a <sound>ko</sound>ala obey at once, curling up on a <sound>to</sound>ffee tin and <sound>no</sound>dding off by the <sound>ree</sound>f.

貪.meaning: A raccoon presses its nose to the fishmonger's glass and stares at the biggest <part>shellfish</part>, a pearl-pink giant. 'Mine. <part>Now</part>,' it whispers, fogging up the glass. It doesn't even like clams. It just has to have it: it <kanji>covet</kanji>s.
貪.on: A <sound>don</sound>key behind it has its eye on the raccoon's hat.
貪.kun: That night it sneaks into a <sound>moo</sound>se's picnic and gobbles his <sound>sa</sound>rdines and his <sound>bo</sound>nsai too.

禍.meaning: A <part>cuckoo clock</part> hangs from a <part>lamppost</part> in the town square. At noon the bird pops out, the clock tips, the lamppost falls into the fountain, and the fountain floods the bakery. One tiny cuckoo, one huge <kanji>calamity</kanji>.
禍.on: A big <sound>ca</sound>rp swims out of the fountain and into the bakery.

瘍.meaning: Rain drips through the <part>leaky shed</part> onto its wooden door all spring, then the <part>sunbeams</part> bake it all summer. The door puffs up so fat it won't shut, with a big round lump in the middle. The carpenter frowns at the <kanji>swelling</kanji>.
瘍.on: He taps the lump and it bounces back at him like a <sound>yo</sound>-yo.
瘍.kun: He rubs it with a <sound>cu</sound>p of <sound>su</sound>ds, but it only gets shinier.

蛍.meaning: A little <part>insect</part> sets off <part>fireworks</part> from its own tail, so its mother throws a <part>blanket</part> over it: 'Not indoors!' The blanket glows green on and off all night like a lamp. Bedtime is hard for a <kanji>firefly</kanji>.
蛍.on: Its birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke needs no candles at all.
蛍.kun: Worn out, it soaks in a <sound>ho</sound>t <sound>tu</sound>b while a <sound>roo</sound>k keeps watch.

倣.meaning: A zookeeper hangs her cap on the <part>coat hook</part> and lets the penguins out, <part>set free</part> for the afternoon. They waddle straight to the hook, each grabs a cap, and they march round the yard with her whistle and clipboard. Penguins love to <kanji>imitate</kanji>.
倣.on: When she sprays them with the <sound>ho</sound>se, they spray her back with beaks full of water.
倣.kun: '<sound>Nah</sound>, stop it,' she laughs, and the penguins all cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!' right back.

畿.meaning: Around the palace, guards plant a <part>spear</part> at the edge of every <part>rice field</part> and tie it with a <part>twist</part> of red ribbon. Everything inside the ribbons belongs to the city: farms, ponds, even the frogs, who now pay taxes. That's the <kanji>capital area</kanji>.
畿.on: In return the frogs get a big brass <sound>key</sound> to the city gate.
畿.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>, mayor!' croaks the biggest frog. He wears a sash of <sound>ya</sound>rn and rides a <sound>ko</sound>ala to work.

瞳.meaning: A <part>juvenile</part> owl at night school stares into a mirror as the lights go off and watches the black dot in each <part>eye</part> swell up huge. It's the best in the class at just one thing: it has the biggest <kanji>pupil</kanji>.
瞳.on: Its teacher rewards it with a lump of cookie <sound>dough</sound>.
瞳.kun: '<sound>Hee</sound>!' giggles the owl, <sound>to</sound>ssing a crumb of it to <sound>me</sound>.

厘.meaning: A farmer builds his <part>farm</part> on a ledge halfway down a <part>cliff</part>. The field is so small that the cow stands on one leg, and he sows exactly three seeds. Every harvest he gets just a <kanji>tiny bit</kanji>.
厘.on: He trades the whole crop at market for one thin brass <sound>rin</sound>g.

桟.meaning: A family of squirrels drags a soldier's old <part>spear rack</part> to a <part>tree</part> and ties its bars into steps and planks all the way up the trunk. Now they can paint the bark from top to bottom. They've built a <kanji>scaffold</kanji>.
桟.on: At the very top, they share a <sound>sun</sound>dae with a cherry on it.
桟.kun: They lay a plank to the next tree, and a <sound>cu</sound>p of <sound>ke</sound>tchup rolls across to the <sound>hu</sound>t where <sound>she</sound> lives: a plank bridge.

挨.meaning: On a rocking deck, a sailor grips the <part>anchor</part> chain and inches toward the darts board, <part>elbow</part> tucked in, one wobbly step at a time. He can't hit it from the far end, so he walks right up and presses the <part>dart</part> in by hand. Bullseye, if you <kanji>approach</kanji> close enough.
挨.on: The board hangs on a mast covered in <sound>i</sound>vy.
挨.kun: '<sound>He</sound> did it! <sound>Rah</sound>!' cheer the crew, and they push open the hatch to tell the captain.

拶.meaning: At <part>evening</part>, a fishing boat races home through the harbour's <part>speed zone</part>, its <part>anchor</part> swinging on the chain. Behind it, a black storm cloud swallows one lighthouse after another. Any second now: everyone can feel the rain <kanji>be imminent</kanji>.
拶.on: The skipper peels a <sound>sats</sound>uma to calm his nerves.
拶.kun: '<sound>Se</sound>nd for <sound>Ma</sound>ma!' he shouts as the cloud draws close.

倹.meaning: A man spends his holiday at a <part>campsite</part> in his own back garden to save money. He hangs his one coat on a <part>coat hook</part> nailed to the fence, cooks beans over a candle and uses the same tea bag five times. He calls himself <kanji>frugal</kanji>.
倹.on: He even rents out his dog's <sound>ken</sound>nel as a spare tent.
倹.kun: At night he sneezes in the cold, '<sound>Tsu</sound>!', and warms his hands on an empty <sound>mu</sound>g.

賦.meaning: A <part>warrior</part> who would rather be a poet goes door to door collecting one <part>shellfish</part> from each family for the king. To soften the blow, he recites a little poem with every one he takes. Still, nobody likes the <kanji>levy</kanji>.
賦.on: Back home he counts the haul lying on his rolled-out <sound>fu</sound>ton.
